# Be kind

https://tellothers.com/be-kind

> Would you rather be clever or kind?

The catch is, you'll never be clever enough. You can be both, of course, and we're all dealt a different hand.

Clever people are a dime a dozen. It's the kind ones who make it to the top, because people want to keep them around.

And it's the kind ones we hang out with: they don't treat anyone like a fool.

Kindness alone won't cut it, though. Be kind on the inside and clever on the outside.

Kindness is like going sober. Stop drinking, and suddenly everyone around you looks drunk. Same with kindness: unkindness jumps right out at you. And to think I used to take all of it at face value.

We go through life with our shields up, braced for whatever hurt other people's words and actions might bring. You can just lower the shield. Don't take anything personally. Let it roll off you like water off a duck's back.

Nobody can offend you. Only you can decide to take offense. Be kinder, and let people be.

Being kind doesn't make you a pushover. The kind are the strong ones, and life is easier for the strong than for the weak — the angry ones.

Being kind is a tool. It tunes you so divine energy comes through with as little distortion as possible.

Loving-kindness is a compass and a lighthouse for every situation. Train it, and things fall into place. The practice has a name: metta.

Let kindness make the call. Watch which gate your thoughts and choices pass through on their way out. Kindness is the only measure. Then do whatever you want.

It's better to be kind.

---

# The universe acts through others

https://tellothers.com/other-people

> Look who it keeps sending you

The secret to steering reality without drawing the attention of the men in white coats is simple. The universe acts through other people. Once you see it, everything becomes obvious.

I'm surrounded by people I love, and they love me back.

I met Alexey Molchanov. He said: "Become an instructor." A year went by, and here I am, a freediving instructor.

Turns out reality keeps offering. I started saying yes to everything. It's the universe giving me a lift. If you've been invited, you've already been taken care of.

People show up in your life to help, to say the thing you needed to hear, or to teach you something. Once you start seeing it, closing yourself off stops making sense. [Everything is a lesson.](https://tellothers.com/everything-is-a-lesson)

The bell for the lesson is an uneasy feeling inside. That's why it matters to stay calm and content — so you don't miss it.

The bell means you're reading or framing the situation wrong. Sometimes it's a signal to see the game, accept it, and just [sit it out](https://tellothers.com/your-game).

[Be kind.](https://tellothers.com/be-kind)

---

# Never dive alone

https://tellothers.com/never-dive-alone

> The first rule in freediving. And in life

Never dive alone. It's the first rule of [freediving](https://tellothers.com/try-freediving), taught before any technique.

Underwater you don't feel yourself blacking out. The lights just go out. Between you and the end there's one thing — a buddy watching you.

So freedivers go in pairs. One goes down, the other meets them at the surface.

Either you're watching someone, or someone's watching you. That's all there is to it.

Same in life. Don't live it alone.

[The universe acts through other people.](https://tellothers.com/other-people)

---

# Tell others

https://tellothers.com/tell-others

> Improve life. Pass it on.

Under everyone's grown-up layers there's a little knot inside that always wanted to be loved. It's the same one in all of us.

Old layers take up the room where joy could be — and nobody even remembers what the fight was about.

Send the good outward — love, thanks, *you matter to me*. It's how you live to the fullest. When you're happy for someone else, you fill the emptiness with love.

If you've learned something about how to live better, your main job is to tell others. Don't keep it to yourself. Don't take it with you. Knowledge stays alive as long as there are people to help it along.

I want to leave a map you can use to get out. The best thing you can do is tell others. Plant a little meadow so someone else can take root.

Tell others.

---

# Couple

https://tellothers.com/couple

> No empty space between you

You become whole in a pair. A pair is when there's no empty space between you.

You're each other's best friends in life. This is the person you want to introduce to everyone.

Always sit at the table so you can see each other. Is the face across from you smiling? That's the main indicator in life.

And for that, there must be nothing left unsaid between you. Whatever piled up — say it. Not "later", not "they already know", not carrying it with you.

Say it to the one who needs to hear it: I love you, thank you, this is what you mean to me.

Don't let conflicts pile up. Something off shows up in the conversation? That's a signal. Talk it all the way through.

Saying it clears the space. And the space fills with love.

[Kids are little versions of us.](https://tellothers.com/children)

---

# Children

https://tellothers.com/children

> They'll turn out like you. Work on yourself

Kids are little versions of us. Do you like being punished and told off?

We have five kids, and I've never once punished or told off any of them.

Bring them into your life and show them how it works. Our job isn't to raise them. It's to teach them to live. We got it all backwards.

I tell them everything straight, and it's great. [Speak about yourself.](https://tellothers.com/speak-about-yourself)

I tell each of them: you're a small person, and I'm your exoskeleton. If something isn't working, just say "I need help," and I'll help.

People have kids while they're still kids themselves. So the growing up is on you. Live so they want to copy you. Take them along, and they'll catch up.

Teach them the main thing: do what you want — just choose what to want.

A parent's main job is to teach them to live without a parent.

Relax. You and your kids will be fine.

---

# Speak about yourself

https://tellothers.com/speak-about-yourself

> Where real conversation starts

We're adults. We don't talk about problems — we just go silent for three days and then reply with a ":)".

A real conversation starts when you start talking about yourself. Everything else is topics: news, other people's business, excuses. You talk with someone, and they say nothing about themselves — and it gets a little sad.

Talking is how you find out what's going on with you.

Opening up is the biggest inner work of all. It takes years: the fear of rejection is one of the strongest fears we have. [For real](https://tellothers.com/for-real), when you talk about yourself, you send signals to your people. [Find your people.](https://tellothers.com/find-your-people)

Once I stopped lying, [especially to myself](https://tellothers.com/do-not-lie), I stopped doing [things I couldn't talk about](https://tellothers.com/integrity).

Speak about yourself. The ones you can do this with are your people.

---

# Find your people

https://tellothers.com/find-your-people

> You can't drag anyone up a level

Nice little planet: wars, feuds, who knows what. The locals are a bit wild, but kind inside. You can find your people.

You can't drag anyone up to a new level. So keep raising your consciousness and look for your people.

And it turns out every level of joy has people just like you. People who love hanging out just as much. And we go all out, because we hang with our own kind. This is my life! These are my friends! Anything goes!

Everything I do is looking for my people. The adventures, the posts, the site — signals to people like me. I want more crazy people. On the same wavelength.

The funny thing is, after a while you find yourself surrounded by whatever you habitually pay attention to.

Go to conferences and parties, see who's doing what, [talk about yourself](https://tellothers.com/speak-about-yourself), meet people. The rest takes care of itself.

You're here to find your people and have a good time.

---

# Work for yourself

https://tellothers.com/work-for-yourself

> Outside, for someone else. Inside, for yourself

Not against work. Against slavery.

The goal isn't to earn. It's to not work.

Three levels:
- **UNDER** — surviving. Just to not...
- **IN** — living. Inside, participating, in the grind.
- **ABOVE** — existing. Separately. Watching and doing what you need.

The goal is ABOVE. Don't get roped in. Don't take it all on yourself. Be OUTSIDE.

There's a kind of torture:

> A person sits in an office for a long, long time, the salary drips onto their card very, very slowly, and they go mad from it.

I worked as a sysadmin once: set everything up, nobody bothered me — I'd come to my office and do remote coding work of my own. When I left, it turned out three months of salary had piled up. I had forgotten about it.

I ran the numbers: from school to retirement you're awake for 39 years. 13 of them go to school, work and the commute, another 6 to cooking, eating and cleaning. Almost half your waking life goes into being able to show up for work again tomorrow.

You don't work for someone. The work works for you. Let it pay for your growth. Let it strengthen you. Let it fund your escape.

Don't fight. Use everything for yourself.

> Find a way to be paid for playing.
>
> — Alan Watts

Either life does you, or you're in it, or you do it.

Work **on** your life, not **in** it.

---

# Choose your games

https://tellothers.com/your-game

> Play where you like the rules

Play where you like the rules. Everywhere else, you can opt out.

I remember cracking up at Berne's "Games People Play" — until I realized all those games are parasites. The win is to notice them and sit them out. You can play anything — why play garbage?

Timothy Leary put it this way: "Turn on, tune in, drop out." Drop out doesn't mean "quit college." It means "don't take part."

You can't quit life.

I'm here. I don't owe them their rituals, and I don't have to do what everyone does.

It's good that you can stay out of hate. You can opt out of an automatic reaction too — at any moment.

[Your remote is in your hands.](https://tellothers.com/click)

---

# No offense

https://tellothers.com/no-offense

> Play for every round

The whole point of game theory: everyone gets to do what they want. I'm OK, and they're OK. If something's needed, we'll work it out.

Negotiating without hard feelings means thinking about every round at once. Play the long game, and people want to play with you again.

Make your move, and that's it. The transaction is final.

No need to fight with everyone. People aren't something you throw away.

> Hate is baggage. Life's too short to be pissed off all the time.
>
> — American History X

[The universe acts through other people.](https://tellothers.com/other-people)

---

# Compound your way out

https://tellothers.com/compound

> 0.1% a day

0.1% a day sounds like nothing. Over a year, it's plus 44%. And 1% a day makes you almost 38 times better in a year: 1.01³⁶⁵ ≈ 37.8.

Just add a little every day, even a tiny bit. Don't look back at where you were: the next step, then the next.

What matters, do every day. What doesn't, don't do at all.

These days I go to the gym in the morning, not chasing records. The only metric is showing up every day.

That's how my instructor course went — I just passed one more thing each time.

The first weeks show nothing. Around day 90 you see it: you were here, now you're way over there.

Anyone can start. Compound interest pays those who keep going.

---

# Money won't stop

https://tellothers.com/money-flow

> What the flow brings you

People say cash flow. What flow?

Picture a river. The current runs toward you, and the current is time. Money you do not have yet floats down it: the salary at the end of the month, the loan coming back, the client's payment. Every sum is an ice floe. One is already in sight, the next is still around the bend.

And each one has a price on it. Pay it calmly — everything has a price.

Your balance is what landed today. The river holds everything else.

Just assume the source is endless.

> Spend your money on the things money can buy. Spend your time on the things money can't buy.

Work is extraction. Make sure you're the one extracting.

Widen the channel. Launch more floes, the ones that bring the next ones. Spend freely. Money is chips in a game: you play them to build a new reality and change the world around you.

> Keep your sh*t in order the money won't stop, pretty soon you will be on top
>
> – Cypress Hill

# Show up

https://tellothers.com/show-up

> Don't be late. Keep your grip

If it's important, do it every day. If it's not important, don't do it at all.

To do everything at once, you have to be lousy at everything. To be great, you have to focus on very few things — most of us can barely handle more than one.

Make yourself a slave to good habits.

Show up. Don't be late. And never let go.

---

# Surrender to the depth

https://tellothers.com/surrender

> Real power is in letting go

When you try to force the depth — willpower, tension — you burn oxygen and surface early. When you let go, relax, surrender to the depth — it takes you in.

Real power is not in control. It's in surrender.

I broke through the layer of fear that surrounded me: whatever happens, happens — not resisting the water, not resisting anything. It all clicked in that moment: 41.5 meters came easy. No panic signals — I'm just flying down.

The body isn't convinced by arguments. It needs a lived moment: I faced it, and nothing happened. You can't understand it. You can only do it. Trust.

Panic comes — don't fight it. Let it pass. And it passes. And you stay calm.

Calm isn't the absence of emotion, like the cartoon monks. It's the state you can act precisely from.

Emotions are waves. They want to move through you. We build them into a prison when we cling or run.

[Go through.](https://tellothers.com/through)

# All for the brain

https://tellothers.com/all-for-the-brain

> Grow your brain, grow your life

The way you start your morning is the connection your brain wires in.

The system works. The brain is plastic, the quantum field is ready to grant wishes. Think in a certain way — you change, and the world around you changes too.

Just move. Forward, toward the light, anywhere. As you move, you snag new connections and shed the ballast. Whatever tears off wasn't needed. What's real stays.

Refusing the new — that's aging. Progress rolls on. Miss it — bye.

*Enjoy yourself, it's later than you think.*

---

# The body is a friend

https://tellothers.com/body-friend

> Feed it, train it, trust it

The body, like good clothes and shoes, should be transparent. Unfelt. Unobtrusive.

Addiction turns the body from a friend into a jailer. It starts ruling the mind and makes you scramble to serve it.

The body is a friend. Sometimes like a dog that grew into a wolf and won't let you leave the house.

Feed it right and train it. Trust it with the routine — it becomes a helper.

---

# Skip breakfast

https://tellothers.com/skip-breakfast

> Eat later

Kids don't want to eat in the morning. We train them — like Pavlov's dog, with carbs. Then they grow up "needing breakfast."

Push lunch back a couple of hours. The body's already doing the work — autophagy, clearing, repairing, resting from constant digestion, burning fat. Eating breakfast tells it to stop.

You're teaching the mind the same thing: to stop obsessing about food. We don't die, we just eat later.

What weight-loss drugs do artificially, your body does for free when you stop interrupting it. Nobody buys "eat less often." A shot — sure.

Train fasted. The body adapts.

I rarely eat. I do push-ups and pull-ups.

I gradually got to one meal a day. Saves time and energy. And you don't get fat.

You wake up fasted. Eat later.

---

# Don't believe your thoughts

https://tellothers.com/dont-believe-thoughts

> You are not the voice in your head

You are not the voice in your head. You're the one who hears it.

Lying down after a shoot, meditating. I'm not this guy — I'm his life.

Look for the one thinking the thoughts — no one's there: that's anatta. The one seeing them is atman.

The illusion isn't the world, as it may seem. The illusion is a film of thoughts laid over the world.

The brain can't stop thinking, the way the stomach can't stop digesting. So you choose what to feed it.

Thinking doesn't solve problems. Thinking creates them.

Think it through properly once — then don't come back to it. Decisions are made once, then they run themselves.

[Sit still.](https://tellothers.com/meditation)

---

# Wake up

https://tellothers.com/wake-up

> You are sleeping

Every night you enter a full-blown hallucination. You see people, places, events. You feel emotions, you talk. And you never doubt it's real. Until you wake up.

What if you're asleep right now? Asleep on the way to work, at work, on the way home. Asleep sitting, standing, walking, driving. The lights are on, but nobody's home.

> You are sleeping  
> You do not want to believe
>
> – PQM

You're driving, and suddenly you realize you haven't been here for the last ten minutes. Caught yourself on autopilot — that's the moment you woke up.

You send a message and get no reply. An hour goes by. Two. And your head is already running a whole series: they're offended, they're ignoring me, I said something wrong. They were just busy. That's how we live — reacting to our thoughts, not to the situation.

You think you're driving this guy. He's driving you.

Thoughts can only say what they already know. They hold you in a Groundhog Day where everything stays the same, and the autopilot switches on.

The autopilot is everyday samsara. Catch it — the circle breaks.

There are moments when you suddenly switch on. You see the sky. You hear the sounds. You feel the air on your skin. That's just you, finally awake.

Whoa — I stepped out and noticed I was gone. Just a camera moving. No thoughts. No body.

At first it lasts seconds. Then minutes. Then you start catching whole chunks of the day when you're actually here. And life becomes different. Not because circumstances changed — because you finally look at them with your own eyes, instead of through the muddy filter of habitual reactions.

Look around: everyone's asleep. Talk to them and they answer, react. Then drift back off.

We sleep through our whole lives face down in the salad, noticing nothing and taking it for the only reality. Then you lift your head and open your eyes — wait, we're at a party! How could I forget?

Be the one who wakes others. Look for the ones who are awake.

---

# What it is

https://tellothers.com/what-it-is

> What isn't there does not exist

The freediving instructor manual says: tell students what to do, not what not to do. You say only what is there. You think about what is there, and what you want to be there. What isn't there does not exist.

Same when you talk [about yourself](https://tellothers.com/speak-about-yourself): not what you don't have, but what you do.

I have poverty. No love. Those words name emptiness. Nothing grows from emptiness.

The universe does not need your rating. There is only what you have.

Describe where your life is going. What happened. What is there. The next steps grow on that by themselves. Then pick the one you like best.

Look at what is.

# The brain is a receiver

https://tellothers.com/brain-receiver

> A glove on the hand of god

What if consciousness is a property of the universe, like a magnetic field?

The brain is a receiver of consciousness. And you are just a glove on the hand of god.

# Question reality

https://tellothers.com/question-reality

> What it seems and what it is

Everything you see, touch and smell is only yourself. You only feel what your body produces when it contacts the world outside. Zero contact with so-called objective reality. You can't be separated from the world, because to yourself you are the whole world.

The matrix is in your head. Not around you. Inside.

Advaita, the teaching that the world can't be divided, means "not two". We're just waves on the surface of the ocean. Fruit on the tree of life.

What you believe in becomes real. We show up to enjoy the game of life. Make it up and believe it. That's how what life seems to be turns into what it is.

Check for yourself. Believing is optional.

Because it all only [seems](https://tellothers.com/for-real).

---

# For real

https://tellothers.com/for-real

> There’s no “real”

Everything that happens seems real. But only you decide which of it is happening to you and which isn’t.

Take problems. Each is either a task with a solution you can apply, or a fact of life, like the weather, that you don’t care about. Pull the good over to your side. Treat the rest as a painted backdrop for the scene.

It doesn’t matter how things are “for real”. Any situation can be turned any way you like.

> I am an old man and have known a great many troubles, but most of them have never happened.

— Mark Twain

For real, all is well, and [everything is a lesson](https://tellothers.com/everything-is-a-lesson). Though there's no "for real".

---

# Watch your mouth

https://tellothers.com/watch-your-mouth

> Words are real. Even though nothing is

Words are real. Even though [nothing is](https://tellothers.com/for-real).

Language is full of words for things that don't exist. Those things show up only because there's a word for them.

Say "problem" and you've programmed yourself for one in advance. Problems don't exist. There are tasks that need solving. Or just a fact of life.

Watch your mouth. Not the talk that goes out — the talk that goes in. Little by little, life starts to straighten out.

# Grow inward

https://tellothers.com/grow-inward

> Base reality is a thin layer

What did all the tripping and enlightening give me? I simply grew inward.

It used to seem that base reality is all there is, and the task is to somehow succeed in it. Turns out it's a thin layer on the surface of... what? That's what I've been trying to understand ever since.

Grow inward.

# The spacesuit

https://tellothers.com/spacesuit

> Decide — it does the rest

The body is a spacesuit — a bulldozer chewing through the bedrock of reality, turning food into energy. The mind is its onboard computer. It reads the sensors, produces images and thoughts, explains what's happening in familiar terms. Thoughts, like a stomach ache, are not your decision.

We watch our life on the inner screen of the spacesuit. It feels like you're doing everything yourself, but the suit decides for you. The joke is, you "decide" exactly what it slips you. And you call those thoughts your own.

We are not lost sinners in a correctional facility — we are the source of consciousness, wearing an astronaut suit to explore reality from the inside.

The suit can be steered by a single thought. Decide something — it does the rest by itself. You can decide as many times as you want.

The moment you stop deciding, the autopilot kicks in.

[What if you're asleep right now?](https://tellothers.com/wake-up)

---

# The parasite

https://tellothers.com/parasite

> It feeds on fear

There's a brain parasite growing in each of us, poisoning our whole lives. Its name is you.

The parasite is a leftover of fear, and fear is what it feeds on. A "problem" is the thing we keep not solving, so the nervous system can stay in its familiar state. A self-fulfilling prophecy.

An inner thermostat: my life is 70% good, just because I decided so, and the other 30% is reserved for problems. When there are no real ones, you fill that space with whatever turns up, so it doesn't sit idle.

The trick is, none of it exists. You produce the unpleasant part yourself, in your head. It's all imagined. You can simply stop watering what you don’t like with attention, so it stops growing.

That's what enlightenment is.

[Just lift your head — you fell asleep at the table.](https://tellothers.com/satori)

---

# See wider

https://tellothers.com/see-wider

> The space of possibilities

The space of possibilities is everything that can happen in the next moment.

The trick: once you start seeing it, you see further. A gift of foresight appears — the ability to sense the consequences of a decision before you've made it.

Your own bubble of reality is blown up around you, and the patterns on it are yours alone. Only what you believe in happens.

You feel the space of possibilities all the time. All that's left is to notice it.

See wider.

---

# Drop suffering

https://tellothers.com/drop-suffering

> Hit, but not wounded

Existence itself carries a taste of dukkha. The brain is wired for dissatisfaction.

The Buddha said: if you get hit by an arrow, don't shoot yourself with a second one. Dukkha is not the outside world — it's the reaction to it.

Everything that wounds, we produce ourselves. The first arrow is what happened. The second is your reaction. Don't shoot the second one. It won't change anything — it'll just hurt more.

Getting hit doesn't mean getting wounded. Pain is unavoidable and comes from outside. Whether you're broken — that's your call.

Frost and wind are outside forces. Suffering is an inside choice.

You need to tell them apart so you can better choose what brings you joy.

Suffering isn't a law of nature. It's a habit you can drop.

Turns out tearing away from suffering doesn't even take much effort. More precisely — tearing the suffering away from yourself.

The second arrow is you. There's no one else.

---

# Reality creator

https://tellothers.com/my-world

> You create it by thinking

The world is a projection of consciousness. You can just imagine a new version of the world and start inhabiting it.

This projection has an ancient name — maya.

I used to dislike this or that.

Now my world is made of things I care about. People I love. Places I love. Things I do. It's small and cozy, and I can describe it. Whatever comes to mind is awesome. Nothing but good. The life I love.

You are the author of your reality, not a victim of circumstance.

Around you there's a kind of thin film, a living universe. Everything you say and do plants seeds in it. You plant yourself.

As above, so below.

As you treat the world, so it treats you.

You are the creator of reality.

Create.

# Think forward

https://tellothers.com/think-forward

> Where is the thought pointing?

Every thought points somewhere. Back, judging what already happened. Or forward, at building a new reality.

Ask a thought what set it off and where it's looking. True thoughts don't start outside. The impulse comes from within.

Whatever pulls you back — fear, doubt, second thoughts — is a lie. A mind game. Real thoughts point forward and make reality better. That's the nature of insight.

You can't focus on what you want and what you don't want at the same time.

Only you know what makes sense. Trust yourself.

Think forward — not from others, but for others.

Keep going at [thinkforward.academy](https://thinkforward.academy)

---

# Go through

https://tellothers.com/through

> Not around the wall — through it

The thought of swimming a hundred meters on one breath makes my stomach drop. I sit on the pool edge, bracing for certain death.

I dive. At 75 meters I hold on to one sentence: this is the worst part, and nothing is going to happen. A hundred. I surface, and the wall is broken.

Certain death turned out to be sensations in the body. You can't argue them away. You have to live through the moment.

The wall isn't an object. It's a process. You pass through it, and it's gone.

[Freediving](https://tellothers.com/try-freediving) and breath-holds teach exactly this. Every new depth, every longer hold, touches what you took for your limits. Then in life, too, you calmly walk toward what once seemed impossible.

It's the same with bad thoughts. You can't switch them off, only let them pass. The fear of bad thoughts is worse than the thoughts. A thought comes and goes. The fear that it might come never leaves.

Catch yourself thinking "what if something goes wrong"? Ask yourself: what would you do if you weren't afraid? Your real life is in the answer.

Go through the fear.

---

# Write

https://tellothers.com/write

> Thoughts in your head aren't yours

Thoughts in your head aren't yours. Someone else's attitudes. Your parents' fears. Catchphrases from childhood. Your exes' voices.

Parasite thoughts always move from outside in. Real ones — from inside out. And to tell one from the other, you first have to catch them.

Until you write your own story, others write it for you. Parents. Society. Anyone who feels like it.

Open a note, title it "What I'm thinking" and start writing.

Garbage comes out first. "Why am I doing this." "This is dumb." "What do I even write." That's the top layer, the foam. Just keep diving. The mind goes quiet and you slip into flow.

Once I sat down and poured out everything that had been rattling around in my head for months. A couple of lines remained. They were about what I actually want.

The little that remains after all the foam — that's you.

---

# Talk yourself out

https://tellothers.com/talk-yourself-out

> Stitch your life together

We'll discuss the world, events, other people. Anything but ourselves — the one thing we actually know.

Once you start talking about yourself, the loose pieces become a story you're in. Telling it stitches the picture together. When you talk to people, talk about yourself.

Words have power. Choose them carefully. The life you describe is the life you live in.

Speak and think only about what is. "Poverty", "lovelessness" — word-masks for absence. You can't build on them. If it isn't in your life, it doesn't exist. Don't describe the holes. You make them, and whatever you build drops through.

You can only build from what is. By telling your life, you create it.

Be precise in your speech.

> The one thing that you have that nobody else has is you. Your voice, your mind, your story, your vision. So write and draw and build and play and dance and live as only you can.
>
> — Neil Gaiman

---

# Store shelves

https://tellothers.com/life-shelves

> Don't take anything past its date

Something new I've been feeling: more and more, life looks like a store shelf. You just pick the storylines.

Storylines, not separate stories. You pick a trajectory, not an episode.

Base reality isn't everything. You don't have to dig through the compost. Pick only the pleasant storylines.

Life becomes a single field, like a supermarket rack, where I pick only what adds joy. There's no expired stuff on the shelves anymore.

---

# Move the locus inside

https://tellothers.com/locate-control-inside

> Least important outside, most important inside

Focus is where your effort points. Locus is where it comes from: the point in your mind where "you" begin.

It's like the needle on a record. Move it to higher frequencies.

I still haven't fully taken in this shift of the locus inside: I'm at the center of my own perception, and everything happens only to me and around me.

The formula: least important outside, most important inside. Low-maintenance, but choosy. Do no harm and don't let yourself be pushed around. Outer lightness, inner firmness.

It only works on joy. While fear is the load-bearing wall, you're big on the outside and hollow inside: you cling to the outside because there's nothing inside to stand on. Fear holds by squeezing, joy by filling.

Power's out — they pulled the meter over an unpaid bill. The bike won't start. Whatever, I'm loving it. What problem?

On fear, the same words sound like a pose. On joy, like a fact.

Move the locus inside.

---

# Doubts are poison

https://tellothers.com/stop-doubting

> Stop doubting

Doubts always sound reasonable. The caring voice of reason: cool down, think logically, the odds are slim. You sit and listen, because it's right.

Doubt wears the mask of intelligence and works as a defense. It's easiest to dismiss the unfamiliar as nonsense.

No amount of proof opens a closed mind. Only an attempt does.

The menu isn't the meal. It's like learning to swim: you have to get in the water yourself.

A year ago I still doubted any of this works. The authority of the Buddha and the scriptures kept me going. So I simply decided to check. It's been a rocket of a year.

Doubts are poison. The antidote is to check for yourself.

---

# Level up

https://tellothers.com/level-up

> From "all for me" to "all for all"

The idea of raising your level of consciousness runs through every religion and philosophy. A movement from "all for me" to "all for all".

You can hear the level in how people talk. "Life sucks." "My life sucks." "I'm ok — you're not" — most people live here. "We're ok — they're not." And the fifth: "everything's good" — no fear, no stress, no conflict there.

To solve a problem, you rise one level above it.

You are the author of your reality, not a victim of circumstances.

---

# Integrity

https://tellothers.com/integrity

> Thoughts, words and deeds that don't drift apart

We're made of layers. The three closest to the surface are thoughts, words and deeds.

Thoughts we choose — we make them inside ourselves. Words are the signals we send. Deeds are where we actually meet the world.

Live so that your thoughts, words and deeds don't drift apart.

You can start simple — [stop fooling yourself](https://tellothers.com/do-not-lie).

---

# Don't lie

https://tellothers.com/do-not-lie

> Especially to yourself

I set myself some rules: don't lie, don't deal with assholes, don't be one.

When I decided not to lie, I stopped doing things I couldn't talk about.

Lying is powerful. You can bend the world with words and get what you want more than once. The bill arrives later. Lie once and you carry two versions — the world as it is, and the story you told. Clarity goes first.

The one you lie to most is yourself. That is the lie that decides for you on the day it matters.

Do not lie. Especially to yourself.

---

# Everything is a lesson

https://tellothers.com/everything-is-a-lesson

> Now figure out which one

Life is a game with learning built in. You can just play, or you can play at building a new game. Either way you keep learning to pull the lesson out of whatever happens.

Every situation is a lesson. The hard part is to see it and understand what it is.

The pain leaves once it teaches you what it came to teach. That's the whole mechanism. [Suffering](https://tellothers.com/suffering) that stays is a lesson not yet taken.

Everything is practice. Everything is a teacher. The world is you, looking at yourself from different angles.

The quality of experience depends on how well you integrated the last one. Do your homework and life gets better. Every single time.

If you feel a bit off, look closer: the lesson is often in what not to do again. Otherwise the universe will teach it once more.

Assume every situation in life leads somewhere good. It all already happened. It is what it is. Train yourself to say "next time" instead of "I should have".

[People show up in your life](https://tellothers.com/other-people) to help, to say the thing you needed to hear, or to teach you something.

Nothing is wasted.

---

# Freedom

https://tellothers.com/freedom

> Be ready

If [life is all we've got](https://tellothers.com/life-is-all-we-got), the thing that matters most in it isn't money. It's freedom — being able to do what you want.

Freedom isn't what you can afford. It's the path you choose when everything is allowed.

Freedom is what's mine. I'd happily work for less money and more freedom.

I don't want to work to buy things I don't need. I work for freedom.

So how do you get there when everything around is this restless?

The world as we knew it a few years ago is over. Everything cheap and easy to get was more the exception than the rule. The only constant in life is change.

Keep your business ready to sell, your home ready for guests, and yourself ready to leave.

Ready to sell means every process is transparent. Ready for guests means nothing extra, nothing lying around. Ready to leave means when the next catastrophe hits, you stand up and walk out.

Stock up on passports and bank accounts in different countries. Don't grow too deep into base reality.

[Harry Browne](https://tellothers.com/how-i-found-freedom): "You're more flexible than the government."

In life you can do anything once you've grown up. If you're asking, you can't.

Freedom isn't something you're given or something taken from you. It's something you take.

---

# Mine joy

https://tellothers.com/mine-joy

> Joy is a choice. Mine it

Joy is what you're born with. Look at kids, puppies, kittens: they're just glad to be alive. Where did it all go? Fear ate it.

Joy doesn't keep, and you can't stockpile it. Mine it daily — it expires at midnight. Happiness is the block reward, the payout for a mined block, just like in Bitcoin. You have to mine it fresh every time. Proof of work is just another word for proof it works.

Suffering for 70 years is too much. Seventy years of fun is barely enough, especially if the fun only started at 40.

It feels like without anxiety you'd go soft. The energy doesn't go anywhere. It just flows toward what you want instead of away from what you fear.

Money solves money problems. What's left are the ones money can't solve. Get happy first.

Want to be happy? Play. Do the things you never got to do as a kid.

The world around me is falling apart, and I can't stop it. But whether I enjoy my life is up to me, not to the world around me. I've tuned mine so that every moment is a joy, and then I widened that little island of sanity. Now everyone who listened is enjoying it with me.

Stop digging into yourself. Dig. Mine it.

Anything other than joy is a lie.

[None of it is for real.](https://tellothers.com/for-real)

---

# Be bored

https://tellothers.com/be-bored

> Interest needs boredom first

"Dad, can I have the iPad? I want to watch cartoons."

Joy is dopamine: you do something, you pull it off, you get the hit. A screen gives you the same hit for nothing. Switch it on and stare.

Parents hand a kid a screen so the kid will leave them alone. The kid ends up pouring all their attention into it. Industry leaders raise their kids without screens.

For interest to show up, you have to be bored, with nothing to do. Boredom is the engine of progress. It's where "I want to make something" comes from.

You need time alone with yourself to invent who you are. Otherwise you're like a dog: the phone screen lights up, you drool.

Be bored.

---

# The day only gets better

https://tellothers.com/the-day-only-gets-better

> Notice it. Say it

Notice that the day is getting better. First thing in the morning. When you notice — say it.

That's the whole practice.

Each moment is the last. Each day. We slip away in thoughts — into yesterday, into the foggy somewhere ahead — while our character keeps living the same today on a loop. Groundhog Day.

And then you start noticing: the day is getting better. And since we're here to have a good time, little by little, you start having one.

You don't have to believe it. The brain imprints whatever you put into words. Saying it out loud is what does the work.

The day is getting better at such a rate that soon it won't stop.

You only have one day. It's always today.

---

# Do what you like

https://tellothers.com/do-what-you-like

> Just want it harder

Life is measured in joy. Joy comes either when something you like happens — that's luck — or, simplest of all, when you do what you want.

For that you have to want it harder.

Life is too short to do what you should. And long enough to do what you want.

I do what I want, and it picks up speed. And I can't fail: what I wanted is already happening. The rest — whatever happens, happens. I do what I want, and the world just glows.

Everything is allowed. Just — don't break anything.

Do what you want. Just want it harder.

---

# Love life

https://tellothers.com/love-life

> Nothing extra. Only what you love

Love life.

The first noble truth of Buddhism: suffering exists. When the Buddha spoke of suffering, he didn't mean an abstract "life is pain" — he meant a concrete list of mental afflictions. Afflictions are contagious. They get into others and play themselves out. It's easy to list what you don't like, what you can't do anymore, what drives you crazy. It's easy to say things aren't going the way they could or the way you wanted. And you can infect others with your version. Meanwhile you're releasing poison into your own aquarium. There's no one else. This is water.

You start to see through the illusion, and that heavy bag you keep dragging around — you can just put it down. You don't need it. It's not there.

You can choose what to let into your life. You keep only what you love. You think only thoughts you love. The rest you just walk past. You become yourself, keeping only what you like.

Try replacing "fine" with "I enjoy it" or "I put up with it" and go through every area. Work: enjoy or put up with? Don't put up with it.

In life, there should be nothing extra. Only what you want. Everything else, for me, simply — does not happen. It's on the other side of the screen. Not on this side. Not on mine.

Nothing extra. Only what you love. People you love. Things you love doing. A life you love. Nothing else needed.

Feel what feels good, sense the good, love what you love. Do what makes you light up.

Love life.

---

# Desire

https://tellothers.com/desire

> The language of the universe

You change the world with what you truly want. When you do what you actually want, the universe starts helping you.

True desire is the language of the universe. It brings joy through the whole process, start to finish. A false one brings no satisfaction even after it comes true.

True desires come from the soul. False ones come from your head and the people around you. From ads. From other people's success stories. From the fear of falling behind.

Do what you want — from the inside, not the outside "I should get some work done" kind.

---

# Best world

https://tellothers.com/best-world

> Live to the fullest

We've been let out to play here for about 70 years. And we spend it suffering, fighting, clinging to animal instincts.

The average life runs on fear as its load-bearing wall. The max life runs on joy.

Standing on the balcony today, thinking: we're finally living the way I wanted. And I felt it — what a life. The door opens, Anya walks in: what a great life we have.

On fear you live on the outside — important, liked, holding it together. Empty inside. On joy it's the opposite: light on the outside, solid inside. Undemanding on the outside because you're choosy inside.

Live your life to the fullest.

---

# Everything is now

https://tellothers.com/dont-wait

> What matters most is right now

There is no tomorrow. It's always today. Look closely, and all there is is an endless now.

The past is memory. The future is imagination. You play them both now.

Life is too short to do what I have to do. It's long enough to do what I want to do.

You can't do anything next year. You can't walk in there and move things around.

Try living just today. You've got about sixteen hours. What can you get done in them?

Try it, say it, go there — now, while the window is open.

Don't wait.

Just [don't get tired](https://tellothers.com/dont-get-tired).

---

# Don't get tired

https://tellothers.com/dont-get-tired

> No resting in the cemetery

Everyone says it: "No time to relax." "I'll sleep when I'm dead." "Plenty of time to rest in the grave."

And at the cemetery there's a sign: "Strictly no resting on cemetery grounds. Fine."

Best reminder I know. Resting is for the living — later it's against the rules.

Don't get tired. Tired, you're just a bag of organs. When you're tired you want nothing, and you still have to keep going. Like surfing: you lose speed, lose the moment, and get buried under everything you have to do. Instead of riding the wave, you drown in it. And we call it fate.

It's convenient to be tired on weekends and "rest" from the week. It's like freediving: if your ears hurt, you should have equalized your ears earlier. Same here: if you're tired, you should have rested earlier.

You don't work music, you play it. It's not a race to the final note. Same with life: it's not about reaching retirement faster.

Rest while you're alive.

---

# Life is all we got

https://tellothers.com/life-is-all-we-got

> Hard? Compared to what?

Life is hard? Compared to what? It's all we've got.

I realized long ago that the very worst life beats none. And that settled it for good.

You can't win at life, period. Nobody wins by having the most money at the end. You win every moment.

We're all going to die, and none of us gets that much. So while we're here, let's have a good time.

Your second life begins when you realize there's only one. And then you realize it's one for all of us.

There's nothing else to do on Earth. Live, and help others live.

[Pass it on.](https://tellothers.com/tell-others)

# Be grateful

https://tellothers.com/be-grateful

> The antidote to everything

Thank life — and it thanks you back. Simple. Always has been.

The good is what's real: joy, love, gratitude. That's how you know what to do. That's you. The rest you can ignore.

Our life is a party on the Titanic. The catch: you're the one steering. The wheel is attention, the engine is gratitude, and joy is the lighthouse. Choose what brings you joy, and be grateful. Find something to be grateful for in what's happening. The universe takes care of the rest.

After a week of gratitude, something started lifting inside me.

I learned to expect nothing and keep my heart open, ready to take whatever may come.

Notice the good — and there will be more of it. It pairs with metta: there you wish the good, here you find it.

Be grateful. It's the antidote to everything.

# English

https://tellothers.com/english

> The operating system of the world

English isn't just a language anymore. It's the operating system of the world.

Everything new shows up in English first. With it, you step out of your local bubble.

Everything is locked behind English. The whole world is.

Learn English. And [read](https://tellothers.com/read).

# Meditation

https://tellothers.com/meditation

> Close your eyes to see

Sit down. Close your eyes. Breathe. Notice you're thinking — return to the breath.

That's the whole technique.

The goal of meditation is not to react. To expand within. The goal of awakening is permanent presence. Remember that you're breathing. Notice your breath throughout the day. It brings you back to the present moment.

Do everything slowly. Do not react. Faster doesn't mean better. [Freediving](https://tellothers.com/try-freediving) teaches that too.

It’s a way to notice that *you are not your thoughts*. Twenty minutes of sitting and you watch the same scripts run on a loop. Meditate longer and you stop confusing the script with yourself.

Keys: love, relaxation, trust, balance, acceptance, letting go, no judgment.

The depth has a map: collectedness is samadhi, observation is vipassana.

Meditation really is a paradoxical life hack — good things happen when you stop trying so hard to make them happen.

Meditation is fasting for the mind.

Try it in the morning, before you reach for the phone.

---

# Try freediving

https://tellothers.com/try-freediving

> A gym for the spirit

Freediving isn't swimming. It isn't even diving. It's training to stay calm.

Anger eats your air. So does irritation. If you can't calm down, you don't dive. Meditate or surface.

You don't force a dive. You let go into it. Every dive should feel light and easy. So should life.

The instructor manual says: tell students what to do, not what to avoid. We aren't teaching freediving. We teach stillness and composure. Control. The deepest control is letting go of it.

When something strange comes up, you relax your mind and drop through it. You fall through the walls inside you without flinching. They dissolve.

When you dive, your character stays on the surface. You sink out of its world into yourself. The mind stops feeding you lines.

The best dive is when you move without thought and think without words. Meditators call it samadhi — you simply disappear.

The depth washes out everything you don't need. Then you choose what to let back in.

Try freediving. It's a gym for the spirit.

Free as in freedom.

---

# Learn Buddhism

https://tellothers.com/learn-buddhism

> Liberation as technology

Buddhism is a manual for how the mind suffers and how to stop it. The most precise psychology I've come across.

I came for the meditation and stayed for the framework. It's called dharma. The way out of the wheel is nirvana.

The whole of Buddhism: suffering is inevitable, but it isn't real. And the entire Eightfold Path comes down to this: live, and don't mess anything up.

The Buddha said: don't take my word for it, check for yourself. Once you start checking, it turns out there's nothing to believe in. Buddhism is a blueprint. Follow its precepts and you become who you were meant to be. You unfold from the inside and finally fill the shape you were always meant to take.

> Paying attention to whatever is happening is mindfulness meditation.

— Robert Wright, [*Why Buddhism Is True*](https://tellothers.com/why-buddhism-is-true)

A technology of liberation. The method works. Start with one book, then sit down and close your eyes.

Buddhism gives you the foundation, the instructions. The last mile you walk yourself.

---

# Try biohacking

https://tellothers.com/biohacking

> Bottom up — from sleep to microdosing

The body is a receiver. Out of tune, it picks up noise, and you think that's what the world sounds like. Tune it, and the signal comes through cleaner.

**Sleep.** The brain washes itself while you sleep.

**Magnesium.** The foundation. My legs cramped for years before I realized I was simply low on it. Magnesium, not magnesia. With lite salt: less sodium, added potassium.

**L-theanine.** Calm without the drowsiness. Great with coffee: it takes the edge off.

**5-HTP.** Fuel for life. I take it for serotonin; it keeps my outlook bright. Days feel lighter, and I sleep better at night.

**Noopept.** A short-acting nootropic that doesn't disturb sleep. It wipes the screen clean. Everything comes into focus. The clutter clears out of your head, and all that's left is taking things in.

**Microdosing.** The top of the stack. A feeling that I can do anything and it will work out. And it does. On microdose days everything flows — fast, clear, sharp. You feel alive.

The goal is a steady good mood and being up for anything.

The path to enlightenment is simple: freediving, meditation, biohacking.

---

# Sobriety

https://tellothers.com/dont-drink

> A clear head is the strongest psychedelic

Alcohol is the only drug where people think you're sick if you DON'T take it.

Say "I don't drink" and the interrogation begins. Why? What happened? Not even on holidays? As if sobriety were a diagnosis. As if turning down poison needs a reason and saying yes doesn't.

The one thing missing from my life is alcohol. It's pure extract of evil. It dissolves the finest neurons and wipes your settings. It's a one-way ticket: you get duller and never notice. You stop feeling life and stop sending a signal.

No alcohol, no cigarettes. Psychedelics, yes.

> The strongest psychedelic is what they call clean living: a sober, reasonably disciplined way of life.

— Victor Pelevin

[Kindness is like going sober: suddenly you notice the unkindness.](https://tellothers.com/be-kind)

# Read

https://tellothers.com/read

> You haven't found out the best part yet

You haven't found out the best part yet.

Reading, you think thoughts you'd never have come up with in your whole life. That's how you make your life.

We live in a tiny piece of the world. The world is endless, and around every corner there's a new one. Read, and your piece grows.

Get used to reading. Then anything you need, you can simply read.

Put the phone down. Switch your mode of consumption to the one that makes you better.

> I never stopped reading. I never stopped listening. I never stopped learning.
>
> — Dan John, *Never Let Go*

# Why Buddhism Is True

https://tellothers.com/why-buddhism-is-true

> Robert Wright. The mind, explained from the inside

Every feeling you trust as information is a setting evolution selected for, not a report on reality.

The book lays out how the mind is built from the Buddhist side. Evolutionary psychology on one page, meditation on the next, the same machine seen from both ends.

It describes what I saw myself. In my own words.

It handed me a thread. I pulled it and dragged myself out.

Nothing new was discovered here. Buddhism was rediscovered — Buddhist psychology, to be exact.

Read it.

---

# How I Found Freedom in an Unfree World

https://tellothers.com/how-i-found-freedom

> Harry Browne. The cage is built out of traps you walk into

Browne takes freedom apart and finds traps. You walk into each one yourself.

The identity trap — living the way people expect you to. The morality trap — living by someone else's rules instead of your own. The group trap — trying to change the world through people who don't want to change. The previous-investment trap — sticking with something because you already paid for it. The certainty trap — holding on to what was true once.

Freedom here is not a revolt and not a move abroad. It is the room to live your life the way you want, starting the moment you stop paying for other people's expectations.

Read it in English. There is no Russian edition.

---

# 12 Rules for Life

https://tellothers.com/12-rules-for-life

> Jordan Peterson. Start with the room, end with the truth

Peterson builds a life out of plain things. Clean your room. Stand up straight. Keep company with people who want the best for you. Tell the truth.

One of the twelve caught me instantly, because it's the main one for me too. Tell the truth, or at least don't lie. Lying is powerful — you can bend the world with words and get what you want more than once. The cost arrives later: fill yourself with lies and, on the day it matters, you won't have the clarity to decide right.

My rule, "don't lie, first of all to yourself", isn't the same as Peterson's "tell the truth, or at least don't lie".

Start here. Read it with someone.

# The Hermit and Six-Toes

https://tellothers.com/the-hermit-and-six-toes

> Pelevin. The sharpest book about waking up is about chickens

The sharpest book about waking up was written about chickens.

Two of them live on a poultry plant. Chickens have a society, a hierarchy, feeders, traditions, leaders, poets, a calendar. And a Wall of the World, behind which, by definition, there is nothing.

Our life is the same plant. Work, mortgage, status, plans. Our own Wall: quit and live how you want, drop the career for something unclear, stop doing what brings no joy. Nothing out there, everyone agrees.

The Hermit and Six-Toes have never flown. They meditate, they invent training routines. Then they catch the simple thing — to fly, you flap your wings, often.

I reread it all the time. A lot is packed in there, and some of it took me years to get.

Two hours to read. Then decide which world you live in.

# Lying

https://tellothers.com/lying

> Sam Harris. Honest people are a shelter

Harris takes the smallest case — the white lie, told to spare someone — and shows the bill.

Every lie splits the world in two: the way things are, and the version you handed over. From then on you maintain both. That upkeep is the price, and it grows.

Honest people become a shelter. You know they won't say one thing to your face and another behind your back, so around them you can stop guarding yourself.

An essay, one sitting. Read it.

# Truth

https://tellothers.com/truth

> Hector Macdonald. The same fact, told many ways

There are many ways to tell the truth. The same fact can be framed to mislead, or to build exactly the illusion you need.

You’ll be misunderstood anyway. What matters is the intent.

# Free Will

https://tellothers.com/free-will

> Sam Harris. The decision lands before you do

Your brain settles the decision before you know about it. What you call choosing is the story told afterwards, fitted to what already happened.

Harris takes that seriously and follows it all the way out. If the thought that moved you arrived on its own, there is no author standing behind it to blame or to congratulate.

Responsibility survives this. What doesn't survive is the hatred you keep for yourself over what you did — and the pride that runs on the same fuel.

Read it.

The story of money: from seashells and beads, through gold, to the money governments print.

Read it to see that money exists only as long as we believe in it.

# Click

https://tellothers.com/click

> The lights are on, but nobody's home

I spent half my life on autopilot. Studied where my parents wanted. Worked wherever would take me. Then I saw my life in a movie.

A remote that fast-forwards through the boring parts. Zip — and you're already further on. Handy. The remote learns your preferences and starts skipping on its own. Whole years — zip.

The remote also has a pause button. Press it — the world freezes, and you notice that you're here.

Instead of replaying past episodes and seasons, grow yourself a remote.

Your remote is in your hands.

# The Matrix

https://tellothers.com/the-matrix

> Waking up into real life

In The Matrix, reality is a grim world at war with machines. And going by the plot, the rebels' world is a matrix too — no way out.

It's the other way around. You wake up from a dull life into the real one. A beautiful one.

I thought leaving the matrix meant leaving the anthill. It turned out to mean feeling like an ant. Seeing that you're conditioned from every side.

You wear the matrix on your head. You can't escape it — it's you. But you can reprogram it.

Start putting your own stuff in. Push the storylines where you want to know what happens next.

[Life is like a store shelf.](https://tellothers.com/life-shelves)

# The Life of Chuck

https://tellothers.com/the-life-of-chuck

> You carry the world in your head

Of all the films of 2025, this one got to me the most — it nails the world we carry around in our heads. I even read Stephen King's original.

An ordinary Thursday. Chuck hears drums and dances in the street. Just because. The one moment in his whole life when the [spacesuit](https://tellothers.com/spacesuit) didn't decide for him.

The screen goes dark — and what's left? That Thursday.

You can know you'll die, promise yourself to live — and still sleep through your whole life.

What would you do if you weren't afraid?

# Soul

https://tellothers.com/soul

> What music is playing inside you

When Pixar made Soul, they spent a long time working out how to draw a soul. The souls they ended up with are kind of faceless. The early version, where the soul is a rainbow, is closer to the truth.

![How Pixar searched for the look of a soul: from rainbow to faceless](https://tellothers.com/images/films/soul.jpg)

It brings to mind true colors. What you're painted with inside.

I like comparing the soul to music even more. If God existed, he'd be something like music: kids hear it and start dancing, nobody has to explain. What music is playing inside you? Which notes sound in it — anger, fear, jealousy? Or joy, love, kindness?

[Joy is a choice.](https://tellothers.com/mine-joy)

# The Village

> Those we don't speak of

Those we don't speak of.

No need to tiptoe around anything.

[Speak about yourself.](https://tellothers.com/speak-about-yourself)
